data.question: Does check_order ignore the diff?

evidence.note: research note CONFIRMED; tests/test_ahead_of_diff.py 2 failed unfixed
brief read: decisions and lessons applied

chunk_findings.detail: The diff handed to `check_order` is the item's diff *at the instant the later gate is requested*, and for the early-refusal path that instant can be one where the item has no changes at all. `_order_refusal`'s own docstring says the check is "asked BEFORE the review is paid for (one run before `implement` reviews an empty diff)", i.e. it exists to refuse precisely when the diff is still empty. With the diff now supplied, an empty diff contains no changed path, so every gate ahead whose `applies_when` is a path glob is classified as not-applicable and is dropped from `order.ahead`; `order.refusal` is then empty and `_order_refusal` returns `None`. Concrete input: an item with nothing changed yet, a `[gates]` config whose order is `lint` (required, `applies_when = ["src/**"]`) before `review`, and a `ddflow review` request; the item diff is empty, `lint` finds no matching path, is treated as N/A, and the `block` refusal that used to fire no longer does — the review (and via `_order_gate`, `gate record`) proceeds on an empty diff. Before this change `check_order` saw no diff, so `lint` stayed ahead and the refusal was produced. The fix is only safe once the item already carries the change set the ahead-gate's `applies_when` is meant to be judged on; at the pre-work/empty-diff point it silently disarms the `block` ordering guarantee.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/review.py:812 (`_order_refusal`; same pattern at ddflow/api/gates.py:284-288 `_order_gate`)

chunk_findings.detail: The final assertion is negative-only and never checks the command actually succeeded or that anything was refused, so it cannot distinguish "no gate ahead" from "the code under change blew up". The captured `code`, `out`, `err` of the `gate record T1 bug_hunt ...` call are used solely as `assert "comes after" not in out + err`. Concrete input: run this test against a build where the new threading is broken, e.g. `status()` is invoked with a `diff` keyword it does not accept, or the lazy `lambda: CM.changed_paths(repo, item)` raises (git index lock, no worktree). `_order_gate` then raises, `run_cli` returns non-zero with a traceback that does not contain the substring `comes after`, and the test passes while the exact behaviour it is meant to pin (`enforce_order = block` no longer refusing on the diff-excused `unit_tests`) is not exercised at all. The same file also has no positive control (a non-excused gate ahead of `bug_hunt` still producing the refusal), so an inverted/early-return regression in `check_order` would be invisible. Adding `assert code == 0, out + err` plus a positive refusal case makes the test non-vacuous.

data.title: ddflow/api/review.py:812 (`_order_refusal`; same pattern at ddflow/api/gates.py:284-288 `_order_gate`)

chunk_findings.detail: The earlier finding was that this test's only assertion is `assert "comes after" not in out + err`, which cannot distinguish "the excused gate was correctly dropped" from "the code under change raised before printing anything". The triage marks it `confirmed` and offers as probe the *new* test `test_block_policy_still_refuses_on_a_gate_the_diff_does_not_excuse`. That probe exercises the non-excused branch: it shows the `"comes after"` string can appear, i.e. the negative assertion has teeth in the refusal case. It does not make the excused-branch test able to detect a crash, so the original defect is untouched: the test still runs `gate record T1 bug_hunt` through `_order_gate` in `ddflow/api/gates.py` and asserts only the absence of a substring. Concrete input that still passes this test while the change is broken: make the new lazy diff raise on the excused path — e.g. `check_order` in the pinned `services/gates/measured.py` still not accepting `diff=` (TypeError), or `changed_paths(repo, it)` raising because the item has no base ref, or `changed_paths` being unbound in `ddflow/api/gates.py` (this diff adds the import only in `ddflow/api/review.py`). In each case the command errors out before emitting `"comes after"`, `out + err` contains no `"comes after"`, and the test stays green — so the change's central promise ("a required gate excused by the actual diff is not ahead") has no end-to-end guard on this branch (`test_an_excused_required_gate_is_not_ahead` exercises `check_order` directly, not the `repo`→`_order_gate`→`changed_paths` wiring). The fix would be to assert the call succeeded / the gate was actually recorded in the excused test itself, not to add a test of the opposite branch.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_ahead_of_diff.py:36-38 (`test_block_policy_does_not_refuse_on_an_excused_gate`)

data.claim: review.triage records any non-empty probe, even a nonexistent test node
data.falsifier: triage with a missing tests/x.py::test_y is refused on unfixed code
data.question: Does triage verify the probe?

chunk_findings.detail:
The bare-name scan runs over the *entire* probe string, so it also matches the basename of the very file named in a node id, which is then treated as a bare test name that must be defined as a function. Concretely, given the perfectly valid probe `pytest tests/test_review_triage.py::test_confirmed`:

- `_NODE.findall` yields `[("tests/test_review_triage.py", "test_confirmed")]`, so `covered == {"test_confirmed"}` (only the *node* part is added; the path stem never is).
- `_BARE_TEST.findall(probe)` yields `["test_review_triage", "test_confirmed"]` (the `\b` boundary matches after the `/`).
- `bare = {"test_review_triage"}`, and no file under `tests/` contains `def/class test_review_triage` (it is a module name, not a symbol), so the function returns `"probe names test 'test_review_triage', but no file under tests/ defines it"`.
- `triage` then returns `bad(...)`, rejecting a probe that names an existing file and an existing test.

Any probe of the form `path/test_<module>.py::test_<fn>` where the module stem is not itself a defined function (i.e. virtually all pytest node ids) is refused, so the new check fails on the legitimate inputs it is supposed to accept. The fix needs to seed `covered` with the node's file stem (e.g. `Path(path).stem`) as well as the node parts, or exclude path components from the bare-name scan.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/review.py:probe_problem (_BARE_TEST / bare-name loop)

chunk_findings.detail: The regression test only exercises the new probe validation through the `confirmed` path; the `--refuted` path is never given a probe that names a non-existent test. The bug being fixed is stated as "`ddflow review triage --confirmed/--refuted` accepts any text as `--probe`, including a test name that does not exist", and the only `refuted` call in this file is `_triage(repo, 2, "refuted", "ran it: nothing there")`, which is a plain command that must be accepted under either the fixed or the unfixed code. Concretely: an implementation that wires the new validation only into the `confirmed` branch (leaving `refuted` accepting `tests/test_nowhere_at_all.py::test_x`) passes this whole file, so the regression test does not close the `--refuted` half of the reported bug. The first test loop should include a `refuted` case with a missing test node and assert the same non-OK / "probe names" outcome and no `review.triaged` event.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_review_triage_probe_exists.py:20-31

ddflow/api/review.py::probe_problem (the `_NODE` loop)

chunk_findings.detail: The bare-name scan treats every `test_\w+` token in the free-text probe as a test name that must be defined as a function under `tests/`. `_PY_PATH.sub` only strips `.py` paths, so any other token beginning `test_` is checked, contradicting the docstring's promise that "the command run" is acceptable. Concrete inputs that are plain commands but are rejected: `make test_all` (matches `test_all`), `./test_suite.sh` (matches `test_suite`), and, most realistically for this repo, `pytest -k test_review_triage`, where `test_review_triage` is the *module* selected by `-k` and no function of that exact name exists, so `probe_problem` returns `"probe names test 'test_review_triage', but no file under tests/ defines it"`. A user who actually ran the command and wrote it in the probe has the triage refused.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/review.py::probe_problem (`_BARE_TEST` scan)

chunk_findings.detail: Previous finding #2 (MEDIUM) was that the new validation is never exercised on the `--refuted` path with a non-existent test name, and it was closed with the probe `tests/test_review_triage_probe_exists.py::test_a_probe_naming_an_existing_test_or_plain_command_is_accepted`. That probe is an *acceptance* test: it asserts that a valid test/command probe is accepted, which is also true on the unfixed code (the old code accepted everything), so it is not a regression test and cannot demonstrate the rejection path at all, let alone the `--refuted` one. The cited evidence does not answer finding #2.

chunk_findings.detail:
`_inherits` grants blanket "benefit of the doubt" to any node whose immediate parent class has *any* bases: for `parts = ["TestAlpha", "test_missing"]` it iterates `parts[:-1]`, finds the `ClassDef TestAlpha`, and returns `True` as soon as `hit.bases` is non-empty, without ever checking that `test_missing` is actually reachable/collectable. So a probe such as `tests/test_mod.py::TestAlpha::test_missing` on a file containing

```python
class TestAlpha(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_one(self): ...
```

is accepted (`_defines` returns False for `test_missing`, but `_inherits` returns True because `TestAlpha` has a base), `probe_problem` returns `""`, and triage records a confirmed finding whose probe names a test that does not exist — the same failure mode as bug Bb049f0ae06, just limited to test classes that inherit (the common `unittest.TestCase` / Django `TestCase` / shared-base style). Previous finding #1 only got fixed for the no-bases example (`class TestAlpha:` / `class TestBeta:` now correctly returns "does not define it"); for a class with bases the fix's own `_inherits` path answers it, so the finding still holds. A stricter check (e.g. verify the name is not defined but also confirm the base chain actually could supply it, or only exempt when the node names a class method whose base is resolvable in-file / is a known test base) would be needed to actually close the bug.

chunk_findings.detail:
`_inherits` returns True as soon as the class that would contain the node's last part has a non-empty `bases` list (`if hit.bases and part == parts[-2]: return True`) — at that point it stops resolving and accepts *any* trailing name. Since `probe_problem` only rejects when both `_defines` and `_inherits` are False, the exact bug Bb049f0ae06 is still reproducible for any test class that derives from a base, e.g. the extremely common `unittest.TestCase`. Concretely, given

    import unittest

    class TestAlpha(unittest.TestCase):
        def test_one(self): ...

    class TestBeta(unittest.TestCase):
        def test_two(self): ...

the probe `tests/test_mod.py::TestAlpha::test_two` (and equally `tests/test_mod.py::TestAlpha::test_zzz_does_not_exist`, or any invented method name) passes: `_defines` correctly returns False (there is no `test_two` in `TestAlpha`), but `_inherits(["TestAlpha", "test_two"])` sees `TestAlpha` has bases and `"TestAlpha" == parts[-2]`, returns True, so `probe_problem` returns `""`, `triage` records the confirmation with a probe that names a test pytest can never collect, and the gate passes. The `_defines` fix therefore does not answer prior finding #1 in the general case; it only closes the no-base variant used in that example, and the fix's own "benefit of the doubt" turns into blanket acceptance of any method name under any derived class.

data.body: regression._member treats an ast.Attribute base such as unittest.TestCase as unknown, so tests/x.py::TestC::test_nonexistent resolves True for bug fixed --regression-test and triage probes. Make a stdlib base (unittest.TestCase, object) contribute no tests. Found by roborev job 2939 on fix-Bb049f0ae06.
data.title: Test-node resolver accepts any method under a class whose base is stdlib (unittest.TestCase)

evidence.note: ruff clean; roborev job 2939 (kilo): 2 findings, the permissive bias is the shared resolver's deliberate design, filed DX-resolver-stdlib-base for stdlib-base strictness; message wording left
